The problem

Downtime is expensive, noisy and slow to fix

Alert storms

One failure fires hundreds of alerts. Engineers drown in noise and miss the real signal.

Slow root cause

Finding why something broke means digging through metrics, logs and traces by hand.

Risky manual fixes

Fixes happen late at night, under pressure, with no guardrails and no audit trail.

Alerts fired per minute while a single service failsillustrative
Every minute a production system is down costs money and customer trust.

04
Chaos engineering

We prove it works by breaking things on purpose

Chaos Mesh injects real failures into the running shop. Every injected fault is logged as ground truth, so we can measure how accurately Sentinels detects and explains it.

Network partition

Cut traffic between services

Pod kill

Terminate containers mid-request

CPU stress

Saturate a service's processor

Ground-truth ledgerRECORDING
TimeInjected faultTargetSentinels saw it
Illustrative entries. Each run's ledger is compared with what the platform reported.

Machine learning

Two models: spot the anomaly, then name it

Isolation Forest

Unsupervised: learns what normal looks like, no labels needed

LightGBM classifier

Names the fault type with a confidence score

CPU stress0%
Memory leak0%
Network0%
Disk full0%
Example output for one incident: CPU stress, 86% confidence

07
RAG SRE agent

An AI SRE that investigates like an engineer

Think

Checkout latency is up. What do the runbooks say?

Act

search_runbooks("cart latency") → ChromaDB

Observe

Runbook match: Redis connection pool exhausted

Verify

query_metrics + query_logs → Prometheus, Loki

Diagnose

Root cause, evidence and a proposed fix
What the agent uses

ChromaDB knowledge base

Runbooks and past incident reports

Local LLM (Ollama)

Reasons step by step, ReAct style

Prometheus metrics

Live numbers for the affected service

Loki logs

Error lines around the incident

Safe remediation

Fixes run with one click, never behind your back

Diagnosis ready

Root cause and a proposed playbook

Operator approves

Safe mode waits for a human

Ansible runs

Redeploy the service, clean the disk

Service restored

Status and history updated

PENDING_APPROVAL
Nothing changes in production without an operator's approval. Rejected fixes are recorded too, so every action has an audit trail.
